sentiment.rationale: IBM raised its full-year free cash flow guidance to above $13.5 billion (from prior expectation of more than $13 billion) and raised its full-year operating pretax margin expansion expectation to about a point (from half a point). Revenue guidance was reaffirmed at 'at least 5 percent' constant currency growth, but management expressed increased confidence, with the CFO stating 'we feel very confident even more confident than 90 days ago.' The guidance raise is organic, driven by productivity initiatives and portfolio mix, not primarily attributed to FX or one-time items. The score is +0.50 because guidance was meaningfully raised on both cash flow and margin, and the improvement is organic.

summary.revenue: $17.0 billion, up 8 percent (5 percent at constant currency).
summary.eps: GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations of $2.31, up 18% year/year; Operating (Non-GAAP) diluted EPS of $2.80, up 15% year/year.
summary.guidance: Full-year 2025: constant currency revenue growth of at least 5 percent; free cash flow now expected to exceed $13.5 billion (raised); operating pretax margin expected to expand by about a point (raised from half a point); software revenue growth approaching double digits; infrastructure expected to contribute about 1.5 points to IBM's revenue growth; consulting growth contribution expected to be prudently cautious. For Q3 2025, management is comfortable with consensus estimates for revenue and profitability.
summary.margin: GAAP gross profit margin 58.8%, up 200 bps year/year; Operating (Non-GAAP) gross profit margin 60.1%, up 230 bps. GAAP pre-tax income margin 15.3%, up 120 bps; Operating pre-tax income margin 18.8%, up 110 bps. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 200 bps.
key_risks: Geopolitical tensions prompting a few clients to move cautiously.
U.S. federal spending was somewhat constrained in the first half.
Consulting revenue flat, impacted by a dynamic demand environment with clients prioritizing cost-efficient high-impact investments and delayed decision-making on discretionary projects.
Transaction processing software declined 2% as clients prioritized hardware spend during the z17 launch cycle.
Distributed infrastructure revenue down 17% due to product cycle dynamics.
Global trade dynamics impacting working capital (supply chain protection).
Foregone interest income from HashiCorp acquisition as a headwind to free cash flow.
key_opportunities: Generative AI book of business now over $7.5 billion inception-to-date, with momentum accelerating quarter over quarter.
Red Hat revenue up 14%, with OpenShift revenue growing over 20% and ARR at $1.7 billion; virtualization opportunity with over $300 million in total bookings.
HashiCorp integration off to a strong start, with bookings accelerated and pipeline 3x last year in the second half.
z17 mainframe launch with strongest ever first-quarter start; 100%+ MIPS capacity shipped; three-to-four-dollar platform multiplier expected to drive future software and services revenue.
Productivity initiatives targeting $4.5 billion in annual run rate savings by end of 2025 (raised from $3.5 billion).
Software mix shift to about 45% of business, with ARR growing 10%.
Consulting backlog of $32 billion, up over 8% at spot rates; net new business penetration up 13% year/year; over 200 new clients acquired in consulting year over year.
Optimism around macro environment: Japan reindustrializing, South Asia booming, Middle East investing, Europe resilient, North America focusing on technology for scaling revenue.
Rational regulation environment for M&A, with optimism that deals will get approved in reasonable time frames.

New AI product advancements: Watson x Orchestra with 150+ prebuilt agents, z17 with Telen two processor enabling 450 billion AI inference operations per day, Power Eleven launch, and DataStax acquisition for real-time data capabilities.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: The CEO stated 'we once again exceeded expectations for revenue, profit and free cash flow' and the CFO said 'we feel very confident even more confident than 90 days ago,' while raising guidance on free cash flow and margin.
